notes: A door opening is cut into the tower (invented, as the door).
The source's one tower solid (pile tip -75 m to the tower top) is cut at +15 m (the IEA's tower base / transition piece height) into the tower and the monopile.
Onshore: the monopile is left out; the tower stands on an invented concrete pedestal, 14 m lower than offshore (hub 136.5 m above the ground).
The bedplate's 2 extra solids of the source (slivers of no volume at its front) are left out.

The source's blades are drawn for a rotor that turns anticlockwise seen from the front (their leading edges point that way at 30, 60 and 90 m); the IEA's turbine, like every big one, turns clockwise. Each blade is mirrored in its own plane through the pitch axis and the shaft: root, length, pre-bend and twist stay, the leading edge leads the clockwise turn.

The source's blade skin is one B-spline of 4,343 x 203 control points, which OpenCascade meshes into 31-79 triangles (the blades were all but invisible); it is rebuilt as a light surface through 121 x 161 points sampled from it (largest deviation 2 mm): 217 k triangles at Draft, 874 k at Normal, 2.2 M at Fine per blade.
The blade is a closed solid: its trailing edge (up to 11.5 mm open in the CAD) closed, flat caps on root and tip (an open skin has no inside for the clash check).

The blade root is made round (r 2540 mm, on the pitch axis) and blended into the CAD's skin over the first 4 m: the CAD's root is 95 mm out of round and 62 mm off its pitch axis, so a pitching blade ran 160 mm into the hub's round ring; the IEA's blade root is circular.
